name: Pale Flesh Color
lede: Pale Flesh Color is a light yellowish pink from Ridgway's 1912 color plates, one of a small family of "flesh" names.

sections.title: A lighter cousin
sections.body:
The library plots this color on Ridgway's 1912 plate XIV, hue 7 prime, tone f, and classifies it under the ISCC-NBS 1955 lists as a light yellowish pink [1]. It is one of a small family of "flesh" names in our data, all built on the same old convention of naming a pale tan after light skin; this library keeps the name as historical, not as a claim about real skin tones [1]. The nearest named color is Pale Vinaceous-Pink, about 1.5 units away by CIEDE2000, close enough that the two are hard to tell apart on screen [1].

Among clearly distinct colors, [[pale-congo-pink|Pale Congo Pink]] sits about 3.2 units off, with [[shrimp-pink|Shrimp Pink]] and [[flesh-pink|Flesh Pink]] close behind it [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 86, chroma 17, hue 46 degrees, Munsell 0.6YR 8.5/3.3 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in only 45 of 23,781 paintings, 0.19 percent, as photographed [2]. It is most over-represented in the 1830s, in 5 of that decade's 663 paintings, about 4 times the expected rate [2]. Korea accounts for the largest single-country share, 1 of the 45, and no painter here carries it more than once [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [2].
